sections.html:
The Wilkes County Register of Deeds is at 500 Court House Drive, Suite 1000, Wilkesboro, NC 28697. Phone 336-651-7351 or fax 336-990-0041. The county page shows hours of Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:55 p.m., closed on holidays.

Tax Administration is in a different building, the Wilkes County Offices at 110 North Street. A seller may need both, or can have an attorney handle the recording while phoning the tax office for figures.

  • Land records: Court House Drive, Suite 1000
  • Tax bills and appeals: North Street
  • Recording deadline for the day: 4:55 p.m.

On a closing day, call ahead if the packet runs long, since pages past the first fifteen of a deed add to the charge.

sections.h2: How far back the records go
sections.html:
Land records begin with the formation of the county in 1778. Birth and death records start in 1913, with a few earlier delayed birth entries, and marriage licenses go back to 1882.

The register takes in deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, assumed names, plats, separation agreements, foreclosures, notary oaths and military discharges. Digitizing is ongoing, so ask how far back a given book is indexed.

On a parcel with deep family ownership, older deeds can describe land by landmarks instead of lot numbers. A survey tied to the current deed saves arguments with a buyer's title examiner.

Heirs sorting an estate often start here, since births, deaths and marriages are on file alongside land records. A short visit with the death certificate and the last recorded deed can show who held title and whether a loan was ever released.

Use wilkesncrod.org, which the register of deeds opened on July 1, 2017. It is the authoritative site for recorded documents.

The tax office runs a second, narrower tool. Its Deed Search holds face pages and legal descriptions of certain deeds scanned for the mapping staff. Signature and notary pages are usually left off, and deeds of trust, satisfactions and wills are not included.

Attorneys and title examiners are told not to rely on it. Treat it as a quick way to find a legal description by book and page, and use the register for the real record.

Once you have the book and page from a prior deed or from the register's own site, you can pull the scanned face page and compare its legal description with your survey. Keep a printout for your attorney.

Recording charges collected in Wilkes County
FilingCharge
Deed, general instrument$26.00 through page 15, then $4.00 a page
Mortgage or deed of trust$64.00 through page 35, then $4.00 a page
Loan releaseNo charge
Plat$21.00 a sheet
Extra instrument within one document$10.00 each

These are the only fees, and they are payable before filing. Ask at the counter what your packet will cost.

The seller does, at the register of deeds, before recording. The state rate is one dollar per five hundred dollars or part of the value of the interest conveyed.

The county general fund keeps half. The balance goes to the state monthly, less refunds and an allowance.

sections.h2: Why recording matters to the buyer
sections.html:
A deed that is never registered loses to lien creditors and to later buyers who paid value, and priority follows the time of registration. That is why lawyers record on the day funds move.

  • Locate paid off loans and confirm releases are on record
  • Get the tax balance from North Street
  • Bring the excise tax with the deed
  • Record the deed ahead of the buyer's loan

The register is chosen by county voters in an election.

North Carolina lets a person gain title by 20 years of possession under known and visible lines and boundaries, adverse to others. On older rural tracts, fences and farm roads may sit off the deed line.

Before listing, pull the vesting deed from the register, order a survey if lines are unclear, and tell your attorney about any neighbor who uses part of the land. A buyer's examiner will find recorded claims, so surprises cost more late.

Work backward from the recording desk. It closes at 4:55 p.m., so a closing that wraps up at four leaves little room for a corrected page.

  • Ask your attorney who will carry the package to Court House Drive, or whether it goes electronically.
  • Check that every signature and notary stamp is complete.
  • Have a check ready for the filing charge if the closing office does not cover it.
  • Keep the recorded copy, with its book and page, for your files.

The tax office's deed search asks for those book and page numbers, so they also help later when you need a legal description for a survey or an insurance form.

sections.h2: Excise tax and the tax value
sections.html: The county estimated that real property values rose about 75% to 80% overall as of January 1, 2025. For recording, though, the price in your contract is what drives the excise tax. The county's tax value does not set it. If your contract price and the county's value differ widely, your attorney can explain why before the deed is drafted.

A short map prevents trips to the wrong building.

  • Deeds, deeds of trust, plats, powers of attorney, foreclosure papers: Register of Deeds, Court House Drive
  • Tax balances, appeals, relief applications, parcel and GIS look-ups: Tax Administration, North Street
  • Court files, estates and wills: Clerk of Superior Court

For any official use of land records, go to the register and the clerk of superior court. Keep the three straight and a sale usually moves without a second visit.

sections.h2: Checking the tax record against the deed
sections.html:
Besides deeds, the register takes foreclosure papers and powers of attorney, which matter when an owner signs by proxy or the lender has begun sale proceedings. The tax office offers a real property search and GIS maps.

To confirm who is on the tax record, search the parcel there, then match it to the recorded deed at wilkesncrod.org. Mismatches usually trace to an unrecorded transfer or a name change.

  • Real property search on the tax site
  • GIS parcel maps
  • Recorded deed at wilkesncrod.org

faqs.q: When does the Wilkes County Register of Deeds close?
faqs.a: At 4:55 p.m., Monday through Friday. The doors open at 8:30 a.m. and close for holidays.

faqs.q: How can I search Wilkes County deeds from home?
faqs.a: Use wilkesncrod.org, the register's site that has been online since July 1, 2017. The tax office also has a limited deed copy tool for finding legal descriptions.

faqs.q: What year do Wilkes County land records start?
faqs.a: 1778, when the county was formed. Births and deaths begin in 1913, and marriage licenses in 1882.

faqs.q: Do I pay to record a loan release in Wilkes County?
faqs.a: No. The statewide fee schedule sets no charge for a satisfaction or cancellation of a mortgage or deed of trust.

faqs.q: Who owes the excise tax on a Wilkes County deed?
faqs.a: The seller. It is paid to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.
